newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile environment board OKs Chilgener power plant.
newsitem.headline: Chile environment board OKs Chilgener power plant.

text.p: Chile's environmental authority said it has given conditional approval to power utility Chilgener's plans to build a gas-fired electricity plant in Santiago.

The approval of the plant's environmental impact study is conditional on Chilgener not exceeding existing emissions levels, the Regional Environment Commission said in a statement. The plant was opposed by environmentalists.
The plant, known as Central Renca, will replace Chilgener's existing coal-fired power station.
The company's plans to build the plant have caused controversy as the result of fears it will add to the city's smog levels, already among the world's worst.
Santiago was declared ozone-saturated earlier this year and officials are working on a new plan to cut air pollution.

"To ensure the fulfillment of the declaration of Santiago as a saturated zone, Central Renca will have to follow a plan to control emissions by monitoring air in the area near the project," said the statement.
